how_to_mine: Follow this plan exactly. Each lens agent reads only its pages (all are in the corpus; read them with `show <source_id> --around TEXT` or `--lines A:B`, tables with `tables <source_id> --index N`), answers its demand items, and records each item in the brief as filled (fact ids), contradicted (what the page says instead) or not-found (where you looked).

Write facts in files of 10 to 25 facts: _build/work/33-api-gateway/facts-<lens>-NN.json, then `facts add --file <that file> --by mine-33-<lens>`. Table rows and value lines: prefer `facts adopt` (--table/--row, --sentence, --heading). Every quote is copied verbatim from the page snapshot (.txt), never from full.md (full.md hits are pointers) and never from memory.

A quote must carry every clause, scope, condition and exception of the claim on its own. When the condition stands in the next sentence or in a table footnote (for example the '*' note under the REST quotas table, line 57), add that sentence as a second evidence item or include it in the quote; otherwise narrow the claim to what the quote says. A universal claim (always, never, only, cannot) with a nearby exception is not allowed.

Fact service key: `api-gateway`. Ids start with `api-gateway-`, for example `api-gateway-rest-payload-size-max`. A fact about another service (Lambda function URLs: `lambda`; ALB Lambda targets: `elb`; AWS WAF: `waf`; Cognito: `cognito`; Route 53: `route53`) is added only after `facts list --service <key>` shows no verified fact that already answers it; reuse the existing id in the demand record (brief.sources.neighbour_facts_to_reuse lists the known ones).

Every hard fact (number, limit, default, price, date, can/cannot, only/always/never) carries `question` (the demand question it answers) and at least two displays for kinds behavior, capability, restriction and default (brief gate B12). A display of a number-free fact is a verbatim phrase of at most 8 words from its quote (RULINGS 2026-10-11).

Quota rows: quote the whole row with `table_header`, and set scope (per account per Region, per API, per stage), default_or_max and adjustable from the 'Can be increased' cell. Keep REST, HTTP and WebSocket values in separate facts with the API type in the claim and the scope.

Changes: a fact touched by a change item sets `changed` (date; old value only if a saved page states it verbatim) and `change_items` (`<history_source_id>#<line>` or the What's New id from `changes for api-gateway`). Current truth comes from the guide and quotas pages; What's New and history rows give dates and deltas only. Anything GA after 2026-07-15 gets the note `not examinable yet`.
Case-study facts have kind `case-study` and a quote of at most 25 words.
Prices: teach dimensions, not rate cards. A rate may enter only as a worked-example fact whose quote holds its condition; prefer the free tier and the dimension sentences.

numbers+changes.label: mine-33-numbers
numbers+changes.job: Every number, limit, default and price dimension of API Gateway (REST, HTTP, WebSocket): adopt rows from the four quota pages first (limits, api-gateway-execution-service-limits-table, http-api-quotas, apigateway-execution-service-websocket-limits-table), then the caching and throttling pages for defaults and ranges, then the pricing page for dimensions and free tier. Then one change fact per change item in d005, d013 to d016 with date and delta, pointing to the current-truth fact. Kinds: limit, quota, default, price, change.
watch: Integration timeout: Regional and private REST rows say 'Yes *', edge-optimized says 'No'; the '*' note (line 57) holds the condition. HTTP API maximum is a separate row on http-api-quotas; WebSocket is a separate row.

Account throttle row: steady-state quota is adjustable; the burst quota is not customer-controlled (text inside the row). The two portal throttle rows are a different scope (portals) and are B-list at most.
The WebSocket message payload row ends with '**': read the footnote under that table and include its condition if the claim uses it.

Cache TTL row: '300 seconds by default and configurable between 0 and 3600'; 'Can be increased' says 'Not for the upper bound (3600)'. Cache capacity sizes come from api-gateway-caching, not the quota page.
Pricing snapshot has no rate card; worked examples only. Do not take a rate from memory.

behavior+decisions.label: mine-33-behavior
behavior+decisions.job: Can / cannot / only / by default claims and decision facts: API types and endpoint types, REST vs HTTP comparison rows, throttling order and the best-effort caveat, usage plans and API keys (not for authentication), every access-control option (resource policies, IAM, Lambda authorizers, Cognito authorizers, JWT authorizers, private APIs and VPC endpoint policies, WAF, mutual TLS), integration types, async Lambda, AWS service integrations, caching behavior, stages and canary releases, WebSocket routes and @connections, custom domains and certificates, CORS, resilience and DNS failover, monitoring, encryption; the whitepaper, decision-guide and Well-Architected decision facts; the comparison facts with Lambda function URLs and ALB Lambda targets; two case-study facts. Kinds: behavior, capability, restriction, default, decision, case-study.
watch: The http-api-vs-rest tables use check marks or Yes/No cells; adopt the row with `--table N --row M` so the header gives the column meaning. One fact per decisive row (WAF, API keys, usage plans, per-client throttling, caching, private endpoint, edge-optimized endpoint, resource policies, JWT authorizer, X-Ray).
d022 best-effort caveat: the throttling and usage plan pages may both say it; take the sentence with its scope and its recommendation (Budgets, WAF) in one or two evidence items.
d028 authorization flow: the outcome tables differ for same-account and cross-account; keep the scope in the claim.
d033 private DNS note: the important-notes page or the private API page may say public endpoints become unreachable from the VPC; quote it with its scope (from that VPC).
Case studies: quote at most 25 words; confirm the quote names API Gateway; the Betterfly page is not usable (redirect).

faq.label: mine-33-faq
faq.job: Verbatim FAQ answers for the FAQ quick-fire section (5 items in the medium template; mine 10 to 15 so the writer can pick) and for the Signals table. Quote whole sentences from the FAQ snapshot. Where an FAQ answer disagrees with the guide or quota pages (for example an older size or timeout), record the guide as current truth and note the FAQ wording in the demand record instead of adding a contradicting fact.
watch: FAQ 63 (WebSocket maximum message size) and FAQ 52/53 (scaling) may state numbers; cross-check against the WebSocket quota table and the account throttle row before adding, and keep the FAQ fact only if it agrees.
FAQ section 'API Gateway Portals' is a 2025-11-19 feature: examinable by date, but low priority; skip unless a quick-fire slot needs it.

rules: Quote from page snapshots only; full.md hits are pointers.
A demand item becomes filled, contradicted (with what the page says) or not-found.
Current truth comes from the guide and quotas pages; What's New rows give dates and deltas only.
Files of 10 to 25 facts; every quote verbatim and complete for its claim; `--by mine-33-<lens>`.
